chunks: Amīr al-mu’minīn said: O enemy of yourself. Certainly, the evil (Satan) has misguided you. Do you feel no pity for your wife and your children? Do you believe that if you use those things which Allāh has made lawful for you, He will dislike you? You are too unimportant for Allāh to do so.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of being stingy with one's family's lawful provision?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) rebukes his companion 'Adi ibn Hatim for excessive asceticism (*zuhd*) that bordered on neglecting family rights, arguing that stinginess is a trap of Satan (*al-khabith*). He clarifies that Allah does not begrudge His servants the enjoyment of lawful provisions, using the rhetorical device of *awla* (a fortiori) to show that if Allah dislikes the withholding of good, He certainly does not dislike the consumption of it by those He loves. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balanced moderation (*wasatiyyah*) between worldly enjoyment and spiritual devotion.
